newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London pulled back from early highs following lower prices in New York despite news of a sharp drop in US green coffee stocks. November was $8 higher at $1,511, while January closed $5 higher at $1,446 per tonne. In New York arabica futures started higher on short-covering on the GCA numbers. But the market soon retreated, pounded by producer hedge selling and local long liquidation ahead of December's first notice day.

The GCA said on November 15 that green coffee supplies in US warehouses fell by 351,600 bags to 1.26 million bags, the lowest level since the GCA began tracking data in 1988. The market had expected the data to show a decline between 200,000 and 300,000 bags. However, most people had expected the stocks to come down, so the impact was not great. The market was nervous ahead of the publication of the latest CSCE certified stock data as there was some talk of supply moving to the board. However, only a modest 1,250 bags of coffee were pending grading last week and hence, it did not come as a surprise that the CSCE reported another slight fall in certified coffee stocks by 150 bags to 321 bags. This is not likely to have any impact on prices, as stocks almost zero anyhow.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks continue to decline falling by 150 60-kg bags in the week ended November 15, to 321 bags (333 bags). This is the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking inventories in 1980. Stocks in New Orleans declined by 150 bags (-50 bags) while stocks in all other locations remained unchanged.

BRAZIL - Brazil's 1997/98 coffee production could fall to 17.3 million 60-kg bags against 24.5 million bags harvested in 1996/97, Edmundo Aguinaldo, head of the Cooperatives Center in the Cerrado area of Minas Gerais state said. The 1996/97 figure is somewhat below other estimates of between 26.0 to 27.5 million bags. Lower production in 1997/98 is mainly the result of the 'off' year in the Brazilian biannual production cycle. However, the fall will be accentuated by trees still showing the effects of two frosts and a drought in 1994 which effectively halved the 1995/96 harvest and from which the Brazilian tree population is still recovering.

UNITED STATES - Green coffee roastings in the United States during the week ended November 9 totalled approximately 365,000 60-kg bags, down from 380,000 bags the previous week and compared with 345,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 14.880 million bags, versus 14.385 million bags in the same year-ago period, it was added.

SWITZERLAND - Switzerland imported 92,841 bags of coffee in September 1996, 6.5 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 842,000 bags, 11.5 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell by 5.1 percent to 1.048 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Uganda (73,100 vs 26,100 bags), Costa Rica (74,900 vs 78,900 bags), Guatemala (63,300 vs 75,300 bags), Brazil (68,400 vs 109,400 bags) and Colombia (103,700 vs 75,300 bags). The country exported 181,500 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 47 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9.5 percent to 184,500 bags.
